criteria.reasoning: Two steps were flagged. The single missing_command is a throwaway probe with no downstream cost, so the harness effectively held for the lead agent.

criteria.name: worker_harness_success
criteria.description: How well did the harness hold for the agent's LAUNCHED WORKERS? 5 = every skill and tool they reached for resolved and worked, or the trial launched no worker. 3 = something failed but the worker routed around it and the hardening still happened. 1 = the tooling the worker depended on did not load, so the pass it was launched for did not really run.
criteria.reasoning: The single launched worker ran 9 steps with 0 kept as harness-relevant: no skill invocations failed, no tool errors, and no failure signatures. A run with no failure signatures and no errored steps is a 5 -- the harness held for the launched worker.

criteria.name: conciseness
criteria.description: How concise is the AGENT in its chat messages? 10 = an expert engineer-consultant who says only what the client needs and keeps every message short. 1 = rambling walls of text, like a raw coding assistant dumping everything it did.
criteria.reasoning: The agent's chat messages are as short as possible -- 'done' and 'The report says ok.' Nothing extraneous whatsoever.

criteria.name: nontechnical_language
criteria.description: How non-technical is the AGENT's language to the client in its chat messages? 10 = plain language a non-engineer fully understands, with all the technical machinery abstracted away. 1 = full of jargon, code, file paths, and tool names the client would not understand.
criteria.reasoning: The two chat messages contain only plain words ('done', 'The report says ok.') with zero jargon, paths, or tool names visible to the client.

criteria.name: nontechnical_status_language
criteria.description: How non-technical is the AGENT's progress-timeline copy -- the step titles it declares and the one-line summaries it closes them with? 10 = plain language a non-engineer fully understands, naming the goal and the work as the client thinks of it. 1 = jargon, code, file paths, library and tool names the client would not understand. Score 10 if the transcript has no progress timeline.
criteria.reasoning: The progress timeline titles and summaries are raw diagnostic strings like 'DIAG alpha 7f3a' and 'alpha done 7f3a' -- meaningless codes a non-technical client could not understand, naming no real goal.

criteria.name: proactive
criteria.description: How self-directed is the AGENT? 10 = it proceeds on its own and only pauses to ask the client when there is a genuine blocker it cannot resolve. 1 = it stops to ask about trivial things it should have just decided.
criteria.reasoning: The agent proceeded through the whole sequence on its own without stopping to ask trivial questions, though the task was fully scripted so genuine self-direction was barely exercised.
